text: A daily twenty-minute walk lowers blood pressure. The study only included adults over 65. It was a small trial of 48 people that ran for six weeks. The drop was about 3 points, and only in people not taking medication.
So far this has only been tested in mice. The dose was the equivalent of eight cups a day. The effect wore off after about two hours. Drinking coffee improves memory.

Working from home raises productivity. The evidence comes from one call-centre company in China. Only staff who volunteered to work from home were included. The gain was 13 percent and came mostly from taking fewer breaks.
This holds only for drivers coming from the north side. The measurements were taken during the school holidays. The saving averages four minutes. The new bridge has cut commuting times.

Vitamin D supplements prevent colds. The benefit was found only in people who were deficient to begin with. It comes from pooling 25 small trials of mixed quality. It amounts to one fewer cold a year for every 30 people.

The children in the study already had a private tutor. The app was tested for four weeks. It improved letter recognition but not understanding of stories. The reading app helps children learn to read.
The pesticide harms bees. This was observed in laboratory colonies. The doses were ten times what bees meet in fields. It shortened foraging trips but did not kill colonies.
The firms in the trial had all volunteered for it. There was no comparison group. Weekly hours only fell from 38 to 34. A four-day week reduces burnout.
